report_title: Final committed result: exact time-window reformulation
reformulation: Time-window fixing and precedence tightening. Of the 4,160 ordered-pair rows T[j]-T[i]+D[i,j]*X[i,i]-60000*X[i,j] >= D[i,j]-60000 (D>0, identity X[i,i] in each row): 3,341 arcs are provably inactive (L[i]+D>U[j]) so their columns, their rows and 2,003 objective entries go; 57 rows are unconditionally satisfied (L[j]-U[i]>=D) and go; the remaining 762 rows are replaced by T[j]-T[i]-M*X[i,j] >= L[j]-U[i] with M=D[i,j]+U[i]-L[j] in [113.7993774414,14386.7993774414]. 130 singleton time-window rows become 65 exact LO/UP pairs, and 65 binary + 65 nonnegativity rows are dropped. 11,090 vars/4,630 rows/41,550 nnz -> 7,749 vars/972 rows/17,654 nnz; integer feasible set and objective preserved pointwise, continuous relaxation strictly stronger under zero-insertion.
claim_class: RPA 6: two integer inclusion claims forming a zero-extension bijection (inverse 1<->0) plus one LP-to-LP inclusion claim whose strictness is certified by a FiberStrictness point with an infeasible-observation-fiber refutation.
claims: Claim 0 {reverse:false, input_integers:true, output_integers:true, objective:'Equal', inverse:1, projection:7,749 pairs, affine_projection:3,341 pairs}: forward integer bijection; block 0 holds 34,620 top-level steps and 46,335 obligations - 3,341 Eq-split zero cases plus the whole target re-derived.

Claim 1 {reverse:true, input/output_integers:true, inverse:0}: reverse integer bijection, 23,194 steps / 56,610 obligations; deleted variables re-enter as 3,341 affine observations `x_i == 0` and the original target rows are cited directly.

Claim 2 {reverse:true, input/output_integers:false, inverse:null}: target->source LP inclusion, 23,194 steps / 37,836 obligations; the only claim a strictness point may reference because the checker rejects integer-declared directions.

Point 0 {FiberStrictness:{inclusion_claim:2}}: 11,090 exact values (identity X on the 105x105 grid, every T at its window lower bound, X[41,41]=X[84,84]=9/10, X[41,84]=X[84,41]=1/10, T[41]=29,425) plus a one-step Lin/Absurd refutation over the fiber observation row of deleted x8861 (0 == 1/10).

Strictness is a projected-LP statement only: the witness has 0 violations in the original 4,630 rows, is infeasible after projection (rows c84/c146 lose the deleted arc) and breaks the tightened retained row c384 by exactly -136077757720947/100000000000.
proof_encoding: 'RPA 6' header plus one compact JSON line of 24,116,589 B with top-level keys claims[3], blocks[3], points[1]; every block ends in Return{map: 7,749 constant/coordinate expressions, checks: [...]}.

Step census by byte scan of cases/test81/proof.rpa: 85,112 'Lin' records, 4,103 'Cases' (3,341 Eq splits for zero arcs + 762 Le splits for replaced rows), 4,865 'Witness' endpoints, 3,342 'Absurd' (3,341 zero-case branches + 1 fiber refutation), 3 'Return'.

Cases records nest their branch steps, so the 81,008 top-level steps (34,620/23,194/23,194) expand to 89,215 step records and 140,781 Return checks (46,335/56,610/37,836); kernel verify reports branches 4,103 and 1,015,224 linear terms.

Both branches of a Le split are emitted as complete sibling derivations; only the untrusted Python generator shares the parent fact dictionary through ChainMap (tools/prepare_test70.py:34-36). The wire format has no shared-fact syntax, so sharing must be decided before emission.
The same claim list is serialized twice from one Python object (request.json 957,603 B and proof.rpa), giving 3,341 affine observation pairs per claim plus 11,090 point values.
agent_manual_work: Wrote an exact MPS reader with fractions.Fraction (accumulated COLUMNS, transposed to rows, checked senses/RHS/markers/BV bounds) plus a second strict fixed-field pass over 26,820 COLUMNS and 2,283 RHS records (digest eval 'Checking source fields and arithmetic witnesses').

Recovered the indexing from incidence, not names: verified the 105x105 assignment grid (row+column sums equal 1) and that all 4,160 four-entry rows satisfy rhs == D-60000 with X[i,j] and X[i,i] in one unit-sum row (digest eval 'Verifying assignment and precedence structure').

Classified all 4,160 arcs by exact window arithmetic: 8,320 inactive binary cases, 3,341 impossible arcs, 57 automatically satisfied rows, 762 retained identities, and checked max(D+U[i]-L[j]) = 52360.6775970459 < 60000 (digest eval 'Proving complete edit scope').

Built the reformulated model and wrote free-format MPS by hand with an exact_decimal serializer (denominator 2^a*5^b, round-trip asserted), then re-parsed it with a second independent grammar and compared rows/mat/bounds/integer/obj/cols (digest eval 'Independently auditing generated MPS').

Found the strictness witness by hand (2x2 swap at X[41,41]/X[41,84]/X[84,41]/X[84,84] with T[41]=29,425), evaluated all 4,630 rows of the original at it, and later mapped it onto the FiberStrictness point (report section 5).
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test81.py is 187 lines and imports across four preparers: parse_mps/row_ref (prepare_affine), expression/plus/mul/expr_json/row_fact/substitute/sha (prepare_test40), SparseBuilder/cases_le_shared (prepare_test70); 785 lines in total for one certificate.
parse() (:12-22) is a shim that strips an explicit OBJSENSE/MIN block by faking a file-like object, because the shared parser predates OBJSENSE; the kernel canonicalizes the untouched source bytes.

zero_case(p,x,packing,old,D,upper_difference) (:26-38): six positional arguments mixing variable ids, fact refs and rationals; emits the Eq Cases with Witness(VarLower) on one side and a four-term Lin Absurd on the other.

prepare() (:41-134): window/pair tables, removed set by name diff (:42-43), Eq-pair packing row (:81), memoized window-difference fact cache (:72-77) and the prove() closure (:96-118) that resolves each obligation by exact residual arithmetic into a direct ref, 'Exact', VarInt or a Lin with a bound ceiling.

main() (:154-183) also owns the harness: RPA/request encoding, canonical+assemble+verify subprocesses, byte-deterministic re-assembly, verify replay and three semantic mutations that must fail with INVALID.
friction: Both failing tool calls of the run were witness bookkeeping, not mathematics: "TypeError: 'Fraction' object is not subscriptable" (a loop reused an arc record name for a Fraction) and a later AssertionError from a reused pair key (digest 'Failing tool results', report section 7).

The violated observation is selected by hard-coded name and value: deleted_positive=a['var_index']['x8861'] with point[deleted_positive]==F(1,10) (tools/prepare_test81.py:146); nothing derives it from the certificate check.

The three negative checks recorded only {"status":"INVALID","message":"INVALID contradiction witness"} (cases/test81/preparation.json negative_checks[0].result), so a mutated term among 89,215 step records is not attributed to a claim/point/step.
Each mutation needed a full assemble+verify pair (6 of the 13 kernel runs) on a 23-24 MB proof, so a single claim or block cannot be re-verified in isolation.

The 4,160 arc rows are classified by three tests recomputed in Python (impossible / automatic / retained: :47, :66, :88) with only counts asserted at :88; the kernel never sees which arcs were fixed versus tightened.
shared_vs_case_specific: test82 is the same source model family and the same 187-line generator with a case flag: tools/prepare_test82.py is 9 lines calling main(82). The case-specific residue is arithmetic, not structure - zero_arcs 3,341 vs 3,315, conditional_M_rows 762 vs 792, automatic_pair_rows 57 vs 53, one dependent equality folded in test82 (dependent_equality_deletions 1 vs 0), RPA version 6 vs 5, and the strictness point present only in test81 (fiber_points 1 vs 0). Artifacts are near-identical in size (proof.rpa 24,116,589 vs 24,094,089 B; request.json 957,603 vs 953,182 B; branches 4,103 vs 4,107), so everything except a handful of numbers and one witness is generic machinery the compiler layer should own.
